court: Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit

issues.label: Meaning of 'to the extent practicable'
issues.why: The court must construe § 6(h)(4)'s exposure-reduction mandate to determine what EPA is required to do.

issues.label: Whether cost justifies declining regulation
issues.why: EPA invoked high cost, so the court must decide whether cost is a permissible 'practicable' consideration under § 6(h)(4).

issues.label: Whether promoting recycling is permissible factor
issues.why: EPA's goal of promoting recycling must be assessed against the statutory command to reduce exposure.

issues.label: 'Low levels' of exposure as basis
issues.why: EPA relied on low exposure levels, which must be evaluated against § 6(h)'s exposure-reduction requirement for PBTs.

issues.label: Adequacy of recycling PPE/warning measures
issues.why: The court must decide whether PPE and signage for the sole pallet company constitute all practicable exposure reduction.

issues.label: Failure to regulate disposal
issues.why: Petitioners challenge EPA's refusal to regulate disposal of decaBDE materials as unlawful under § 6(h).

issues.label: Reliance on RCRA compliance
issues.why: Whether EPA's invocation of RCRA justifies declining TSCA disposal regulation must be assessed.

issues.label: Article exemption from wastewater prohibition
issues.why: The court must determine whether excluding articles from water-discharge limits satisfies § 6(h)(4).

issues.label: Failure to regulate sewage sludge fertilizer
issues.why: EPA declined to regulate contaminated sludge, which must be reviewed for legal sufficiency.

issues.label: Whether staged regulation is permissible
issues.why: EPA relies on Bluewater Network to defend phased regulation, which the court must evaluate against § 6(h).

issues.label: Reasoned explanation / arbitrary-and-capricious review
issues.why: The court must assess whether EPA adequately justified its choices under APA standards.

issues.label: Standard of review under TSCA
issues.why: The court must identify the applicable standard of review for § 6 rules (substantial evidence vs. arbitrary-and-capricious).

issues.label: Adequacy of notice-and-comment procedure
issues.why: Whether EPA satisfied § 553 and TSCA procedural requirements for the 2024 amendments must be considered.

issues.label: Definition of 'article' and scope
issues.why: The regulatory definition of 'article' shapes which exposures EPA regulated and must be interpreted.

issues.label: Status of remanded 2021 Rule
issues.why: The court must decide how the voluntarily-remanded, abeyance-held 2021 Rule interacts with review of the 2024 Rule.

issues.label: Standing and ripeness
issues.why: The court must confirm petitioners' standing and that the challenges are justiciable.

issues.label: Timeliness of petitions
issues.why: The court must verify both petitions were timely filed under TSCA's review provisions.

issues.label: Appropriate remedy: remand without vacatur
issues.why: The court must decide whether to remand without vacatur and whether to impose deadlines as requested.

issues.label: Deference owed to EPA interpretation
issues.why: Post-Loper Bright, the court must determine how much weight EPA's statutory interpretation receives.

issues.label: Whether omitted exposures were 'determined' risks
issues.why: Section 6(h)(4) requires addressing risks EPA determines are presented; whether EPA made such determinations for disputed areas matters.

issues.label: Effect of no required risk evaluation
issues.why: Section 6(h)(2) waives risk evaluation, affecting what record support EPA must provide for its choices.

issues.label: Scope of § 6(a) regulatory tools available
issues.why: The court must consider whether disposal, discharge, and sludge fall within § 6(a) tools EPA could deploy.
